parts.note: to do someone is to impersonate them
mini means little
john and can are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to do an impression of Little John, Robin Hood's friar-adjacent companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little John' looks like Robin Hood's man, but it splits into two pieces: little and john.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a friar of the Order of Preachers, and friars are addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Opener in difficulty to collect duck

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, taken here from difficulty

parts.note: to rake in or rake up is to collect

explanation.surface: A batsman in trouble at the start of an innings is out for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (opener, duck, collect) is a false trail; the duck is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, so the answer is an example of the bird defined.

clue.text: Potty covered in hair, as an artefact

indicators.note: one piece is covered in another, so the word for potty sits inside the word for hair

parts.note: a mane is a head of long hair
potty means crazy, mad

explanation.surface: A potty found buried under hair is described as an ancient artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by people rather than nature, which is what the hyphenated adjective says.

clue.text: Swedish chemist knocking up supermodel once

indicators.note: in a down light, knocking up means the name is turned so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: Yasmin Le Bon was a supermodel of the 1980s and 90s

explanation.surface: A Swedish scientist is scandalously said to have got a former supermodel pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking up' reads as getting someone pregnant; in a down clue it means writing the name upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel was the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite and endowed the prizes.

clue.text: Dumping grounds dry up, one of those filled with sewage

definitions.text: one of those filled with sewage

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the combined pieces are written from the bottom

parts.note: in British English a tip is a rubbish dump
sec is the French wine term for dry

explanation.surface: Rubbish dumps run dry, and one of them turns out to be full of sewage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of those' points back to the dumping grounds: the answer is one such ground, filled with sewage. 'Up' turns TIPSSEC round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspit is a pit for holding sewage and waste, a sort of dumping ground for it.

definitions.meaning: a jokey way of saying myself, the most important person

explanation.surface: A letter signed off politely, then a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one means oneself (looking after number one) and also the record at the top of the charts.

clue.text: Itinerant forgetting piano at end of two dances

indicators.note: forgetting says letters are dropped from the dance names
at end of places the dropped letter at the tail of each dance

parts.note: a hop and a bop are both dances
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft; one goes from each dance

explanation.surface: A wanderer drifts between two dances without the pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: The P for piano comes off the end of both dances, leaving HO and BO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a homeless wandering worker, so as a noun it names an itinerant.

indicators.note: to pot is to put into a container, so the chamber holds the other word

parts.note: a hall is a large room or chamber
antique means old

explanation.surface: A bag of antique chamber pots, as at a car-boot sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chamber pots' reads as one thing; split, 'pots' is the verb putting one word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travelling bag.

clue.text: Yikes, buzzer has caught its owner?

indicators.note: one word has caught another, holding it inside

parts.note: a beeper is a buzzing pager
eek is a cry of alarm like yikes

explanation.surface: Someone yelps as a buzzing insect is caught, and wonders who keeps it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'buzzer' read as a bee: the person keeping the bees owns it.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper keeps hives, so is in a sense the owner of a buzzing insect.

indicators.note: one word punching into another goes inside it

parts.note: canis is the Latin, ancient word for a dog
to cop is to catch, nab

explanation.surface: A police officer hits an old dog over some grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' as a slang term for the drug, not the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for marijuana, the drug from the hemp plant.

definitions.note: the dots carry over grass, the definition in the previous clue

indicators.note: the police word holds the other one inside, as if under arrest

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: Continuing: the grass that's bad gets the cannabis dealer arrested by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is borrowed: the dots link back to 'grass' at the end of 8 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Millet is a cereal grass grown for its small seeds.

definitions.meaning: a particular is a single item or point, as in 'in every particular'
to dock an animal is to cut off its tail

explanation.surface: A specific harbour is asked about.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a particular point, and docking a tail literally removes the tail, so de-tails it.

clue.text: Freshly papered walls in rectory originally …

definitions.note: the dots carry the definition fabricated over from the next clue

indicators.note: one set of letters walls in another, enclosing it
freshly means anew, so the letters are made into a fresh order
originally points to the first letter of rectory

explanation.surface: The rectory walls have been freshly papered, ready for the visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly' makes PREPAED from papered; 'walls in' puts R inside. The definition is 'fabricated' in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fabricated has been made, readied in advance, so prepared fits as a past participle.

explanation.surface: Continuing the rectory scene: the story was fabricated, and someone is delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Made up means invented or untrue; in British slang made up also means thrilled.

clue.text: A sovereign I preserve in instant coffee

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the word for instant

parts.note: mo is short for moment, an instant
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
to can food is to preserve it

explanation.surface: Someone pockets a gold coin and makes instant coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant coffee' looks like one phrase, but 'instant' is a piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a style of coffee.

definitions.meaning: the late Duke of Edinburgh by his short first name, a conjunction, then the Queen's royal cypher
commit adultery, have affairs: a plural verb

explanation.surface: Gossip claims a royal couple are unfaithful to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a pair of royals, the answer splits into PHIL (Prince Philip), AND, ER (the Queen); with a plural subject it is the verb for straying.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual affairs, to be unfaithful to a partner.

indicators.note: dunking puts the bread inside the drink, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A writer dunks bread into a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was the Victorian novelist of the Barsetshire books.

clue.text: State again reviewing repeated notes in paper

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the quantity of paper

parts.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper

indicators.note: reviewing, read as re-viewing, says the word is looked at backwards

parts.note: a riff is a short repeated phrase in music

explanation.surface: A music critic restates their view after reviewing a repetitive score in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' is read as re-viewing, looking again backwards; 'repeated notes' is a musical riff, not a reprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To reaffirm is to assert or declare something once more.

parts.note: to fuse is to join together
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Change unit to join a fight, as a soldier might.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuse box houses the switches and fuses of a building's electrical circuit.

clue.text: Girl expecting bread called for milk, perhaps?

parts.note: Mia is a girl's name
bread is slang for money; someone owed money is expecting it

explanation.surface: A pregnant girl, waiting for her bread, asks for milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expecting' suggests pregnancy; here it is waiting for money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat miaows when it wants milk, so the answer is one way of calling for it.

indicators.note: somewhat lacking says the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the end is the conclusion
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: A disappointing finale lacks heart, yet the crowd calls for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking heart' wants to remove a middle letter; instead 'somewhat lacking' trims END to EN and 'heart' is CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience shouts for an encore when it wants a performer to play again.

indicators.note: on attaches the youngster to the reservation people, so the young one comes second

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people, some living on reservations
a pup is a young animal or a cheeky youngster

explanation.surface: A young person from a reservation is menacing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a Cree person is merely one who might live on a reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangers that creep up loom gradually, threatening without being noticed.

parts.note: kin means family

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A family has squandered its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' scrambles HAS into SHA; 'it' is SA, sex appeal, a crossword convention. 'Capital' looks like money.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinshasa is the capital city of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, so the boat holds the numeral

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Fishermen on a boat net five carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' is the verb, to complain, not the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To kvetch is to complain persistently, as to carp does.

clue.text: Money turning up in Copenhagen or Kolding

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit within the words of the two Danish place names

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Money turns up in one of two Danish cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the concealment: 'in' signals it. 'turning up' reads ENORK upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency of Denmark, where both cities are.

clue.text: Official announcer in Cork I hear regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: A man in Cork hears an official making announcements.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was the official who made public announcements in the street.

parts.note: a bar is a stick or rod
a bed is the bottom of a sea or river

explanation.surface: Something is stuck to someone's bottom, painfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed remark is wounding, as a hook's barb wounds.

clue.text: Setter's dropping weight initially, so I hope that's shifted

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of weight
shifted means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter hopes to lose weight and that it will shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the compiler and also the dog, whose dropping is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoopsie is a coy word for a dog's mess, and an Irish setter is a dog.

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard spoken

parts.note: Cokes are fizzy colas

explanation.surface: A craving for fizzy drinks, as reported.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to urge or persuade gently.

clue.text: Native of central America in rare shower

parts.note: rare steak is red in the middle
to pepper is to shower, as with shot

explanation.surface: A Central American found in a rare rainstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' suggests a person; it is a plant, the capsicum.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum peppers originated in the Americas, so the vegetable is a native there.
